text:
sanjay: Heads up — our canary deploy for the GPU nodepool in us-west1 is stuck because the remote TF lock isn't releasing. Argo canary paused, helm reconcile waiting, and the cluster autoscaler is flapping nodes. Anyone seen a GCS lock object not releasing before?

maya: I see the same alerts. Autoscaler churn is causing a cost blip in the last 20m. Any `terraform apply` errors in CI logs?

sanjay: CI shows `Error: remote state lock not released` and GCS returned 409 precondition failed. The pipeline finished but the lock file still exists with an older generation. I tried `terraform force-unlock` locally but don't want to do that mid-canary without a plan.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout 2026-03-20T15:23 initiated for gpu-pool (canary/42).

tia: Don't force-unlock blind. Check if any gitops/ci runner is still in `apply` state. Look at the `gitops-sync-canary` k8s job in infra namespace — it might be hung waiting on provider calls.

leo: Found a clue: yesterday we imported a nodepool as `google_container_node_pool.imported_gpu` and during the import a state move happened across workspaces. The imported resource has a provider region mismatch (us-west1 vs us-west2) and that left the module in a half-migrated state. When Argo triggered the canary it tried to taint & replace, and TF held the lock waiting for the import to finish.

sanjay: Right — the migration script did a `terraform state mv` + `terraform import` in quick succession from parallel CI jobs. Looks like the backend object generation changed while the importer retried, leaving a stale lock entry. Logs show repeated `retrying due to lock` and long sleeps until TTL.

maya: Proposed recovery: snapshot the state (`gsutil cp gs://redwood-tfstate/prod/gpu.tfstate /tmp/gpu.tfstate.bak`), download and inspect `terraform state list` locally, then coordinate a short maintenance window to force-unlock and run a single controlled `apply`. I'll mute autoscaler alerts and pause the canary in Argo. @ops-bot can you disable autoscaler on the pool for 10m?

ops-bot: ops-bot: autoscaler disable requested by maya for gpu-pool until 15:40 UTC.

tia: After pausing canary in Argo, one operator should verify no active `terraform apply` processes (CI jobs 399/400/401) and then run `terraform force-unlock <LOCK_ID>` from a trusted runner. Immediately follow with `terraform plan` and `apply` in the same runner. If anything looks off, revert to the snapshot.

leo: Also saw extra metadata on the backend object: `migrated-by: ci-run-398`. That matches the migration PR. Looks like the migration script didn't wait for backend generation to stabilize before doing the import. I'll add a guard to block concurrent state mv/import operations and add a check for backend generation bumps.

sanjay: Plan agreed: I'll pause the canary, take a final state snapshot, coordinate a single operator (me) to force-unlock after confirming CI is idle, then run plan+apply from one runner. Post-incident: add a GitHub check to prevent concurrent state ops and update the migration runbook.

maya: :thumbsup: I'll keep an eye on billing and re-enable autoscaler after the cluster stabilizes. Adding steps to the runbook now.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary paused by sanjay. Note: manual unlock in progress.
